record.paper_title: Towards Event-Triggered NMPC for Efficient 6G Communications: Experimental Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Energy-aware event-triggered networked control with 5G RedCap
record.original_question: For networked control systems in which sensors, actuators, plants, and controllers communicate over wireless networks, how can event-triggered control be designed and evaluated so that it reduces energy consumption and extends battery life while preserving control performance? In particular, how can 5G Reduced Capability (RedCap) devices, which support lower data-rate communication and long power-saving inactive periods while retaining cell-side context for quick wake-up, be used so that a device stays inactive until a new control event occurs, and how should the controller and network be co-designed to optimize communication-resource utilization and minimize energy consumption?

evidence.quote: Even for the control benchmark of swinging up and stabilizing an inverted pendulum at its upper equilibrium, event-triggered control reduces communication demand to 61 % compared to periodic control while maintaining similar control performance.

Future work will investigate the impact of event-triggered control on energy consumption and battery life in networked control systems. This can be explored using 5G RedCap (Reduced Capability) devices, which enable efficient communication with lower data rate requirements, thereby extending battery life.

These devices are able to traverse into a power-saving state for a long time during a period of inactivity. Specifically, a device keeps its context on cell side and can quickly wake up for data transmission to transmit data without establishing a new connection. An event-triggered control strategy could leverage this feature by keeping the device in an inactive state until a new event occurs.
Ultimately, the co-design of the controller and the network should prioritize optimizing resource utilization, thereby minimizing energy consumption.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a networked control system in which a physical plant, its sensors and actuators, and a remote controller exchange information over a wireless communication link. Let the plant dynamics be modeled in discrete time by x_{k+1} = f(x_k, u_k, w_k), where x_k is the state, u_k the control input applied through the actuator, and w_k a disturbance. Sensors transmit measurements y_k = h(x_k, v_k) to the controller, and the controller transmits control commands u_k back to the actuator; each transmission consumes communication resources and energy at the wireless device.

An event-triggered control policy is specified by a triggering rule \tau: a transmission is initiated at time k if and only if a triggering condition g(x_k, x_{\hat k}, k) \ge 0 is satisfied, where \hat k denotes the time of the most recent transmission. Between transmissions, the device may enter a low-power inactive state retaining its connection context (as in the 5G Reduced Capability device model), and wakes up only to transmit when an event is triggered; the per-step energy cost is E_\mathrm{active} while transmitting or active and E_\mathrm{inactive} \ll E_\mathrm{active} when inactive. Let J_\mathrm{ctrl}(\tau) denote a control-performance cost (for example, the expected long-run-average tracking or stabilization cost) and let E_\mathrm{tot}(\tau) denote the expected total energy consumption (or, equivalently, expected battery lifetime).

Problem. Design, and rigorously analyze, a co-design framework for the triggering rule g, the feedback controller, and the network access/idle-mode parameters that:

(a) Provides a closed-form or constructive event-triggering policy \tau^* that for a prescribed performance bound J_\mathrm{ctrl}(\tau) \le \bar J minimizes E_\mathrm{tot}(\tau), exploiting prolonged inactive periods of the device with quick context-preserving wake-up.

(b) Establishes stability (e.g. input-to-state or mean-square stability) of the closed-loop system under \tau^* together with quantitative bounds on the average inter-event time and on the energy savings relative to periodic transmission at a comparable performance level.

(c) Characterizes the optimal trade-off curve between J_\mathrm{ctrl} and E_\mathrm{tot}, and gives sufficient conditions under which event-triggered operation strictly dominates any periodic scheme in this trade-off.

Provide such a co-design together with proofs of stability, performance bounds, and energy-optimality, applicable in particular to benchmark nonlinear systems such as the inverted pendulum swing-up and stabilization task.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a future-work/open research direction concerning co-design of event-triggered control with low-power 5G RedCap devices. While event-triggered control and its stability/performance trade-offs are an established research area, a complete co-design framework that jointly optimizes controller and 5G RedCap idle-mode parameters for energy minimization with provable performance guarantees does not appear to have been resolved in the literature as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Event-Triggered Control: Overview
status_evidence.snippet: Future work will investigate the impact of event-triggered control on energy consumption and battery life in networked control systems via 5G RedCap.
status_evidence.claim: The co-design question is explicitly posed as open future work.
